question: An engineer is implementing a Cisco ACI fabric and must use a static VLAN range as part of a VMM deployment. The static VLAN must be incorporated into the dynamic VLAN pool. The existing VLAN pool is set for dynamic allocation. Which action accomplishes this goal?
options: Create a static reservation within the dynamic VLAN pool.
Change the existing VLAN pool to static allocation mode.
Add the VLAN to the pool configured with Inherit Allocation Mode from parent.
Add a static VLAN allocation range to the VLAN pool.
theory: ACI VLAN pools can contain multiple encapsulation blocks, and each block independently carries its own allocation mode — static or dynamic — rather than the pool itself being locked into a single mode. So a pool generally used for dynamic VMM allocation can still contain an additional VLAN block explicitly added as static allocation, without converting the whole pool to static (which would break the existing dynamic VMM behavior) or nesting a static reservation inside the dynamic range. Simply adding a new static allocation range alongside the existing dynamic range within the same VLAN pool is the correct approach. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 4 — ACI VLAN Pools: Static and Dynamic Allocation Blocks)
